title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)
summary: Untrusted data is included in a web page without context-appropriate output encoding or sanitization, allowing script execution in a victim's browser.
impact: Session theft, data exposure, or actions performed as the user.
mitigation: Use framework auto-escaping; avoid injecting untrusted strings into HTML; use context-aware encoding and a restrictive Content Security Policy as defense in depth.

title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (SQL Injection)
summary: Untrusted input is concatenated into an SQL statement instead of being safely bound as data.
impact: Unauthorized data access or modification, authentication bypass, and potential database compromise.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements; do not build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.

title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
summary: Externally influenced data reaches an operating-system command interpreter without safe argument handling.
impact: Command execution with the application's privileges.
mitigation: Avoid shell invocation; use APIs instead of commands or pass an argument array with shell execution disabled and validate inputs.

title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)
summary: User-controlled path segments allow access outside the intended directory, such as through ../ sequences or absolute paths.
impact: Unauthorized file read, overwrite, or deletion.
mitigation: Resolve paths against a fixed base directory, verify the normalized result remains inside that base, and reject unexpected path forms.

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
summary: Passwords, API keys, tokens, or other credentials are embedded directly in source code.
impact: Credentials may leak through source control, builds, or logs and allow unauthorized access.
mitigation: Load secrets from a secrets manager or server-side environment variables, rotate exposed credentials, and keep secret files out of version control.

title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
summary: A sensitive operation can be invoked without verifying the identity of the caller.
impact: Unauthorized users may invoke privileged functionality.
mitigation: Enforce authentication at the server boundary and authorize every sensitive action; do not rely on client-side checks.

title: Missing Authorization
summary: The application fails to check whether an authenticated user is permitted to access a resource or perform an action.
impact: Horizontal or vertical privilege escalation and unauthorized data access.
mitigation: Perform server-side authorization checks for every object and operation, using the authenticated principal and resource ownership/policy.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
summary: Untrusted serialized data is deserialized into objects in a way that can execute code or create dangerous object states.
impact: Remote code execution, denial of service, or logic manipulation depending on the deserializer.
mitigation: Avoid unsafe native object deserialization for untrusted input; use constrained data formats and strict schema validation.

title: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
summary: The code uses cryptographic algorithms or modes considered weak for the intended purpose.
impact: Confidentiality or integrity protections may be weakened.
mitigation: Use modern vetted cryptographic libraries and current algorithms; avoid MD5/SHA-1 for security-sensitive hashing and do not design custom cryptography.

title: OWASP Top Ten 2004 Category A9 - Denial of Service
summary: Resource consumption or algorithmic behavior can allow an attacker to exhaust service resources.
mitigation: Bound input sizes and computation, add timeouts and resource limits, and avoid unbounded recursion or allocations on untrusted input.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
summary: A server fetches a URL supplied or influenced by a user without restricting destinations, enabling requests to internal or privileged services.
impact: Access to internal services, cloud metadata, or restricted network resources.
mitigation: Use strict allow-lists for schemes, hostnames, and resolved IP addresses; block private/link-local ranges and re-check redirects.

title: Out-of-bounds Read
summary: A program reads memory outside an intended buffer or object boundary.
impact: Crashes, information disclosure, or undefined behavior.
mitigation: Validate indices and lengths, use safe abstractions, and avoid unchecked pointer arithmetic.

title: Out-of-bounds Write
summary: A program writes outside the bounds of an allocated buffer or object.
impact: Memory corruption, crashes, or potentially code execution.
mitigation: Validate lengths and bounds, prefer memory-safe abstractions, and use sanitizers during testing.

title: NULL Pointer Dereference
summary: A NULL pointer is dereferenced without checking that it points to a valid object.
mitigation: Validate pointer values before dereferencing and use safer ownership/type patterns where available.

title: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
summary: A password is stored using a fast unsalted hash instead of a password-hashing scheme designed to resist guessing attacks.
impact: Stolen password hashes can be cracked efficiently and identical passwords produce identical hashes.
mitigation: Use Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt, or PBKDF2 with per-password salts and suitable work factors.
